blocks.text: The long docstring names the four-step default check, the two optional sub-commands, and the distinction between strict and tolerant validation. It also declares this file's role as the shared import entry point for both the client and server test suites.
blocks.title: Module-level contract and security stance

blocks.text: Imports jsonschema and referencing at module level with a friendly error message for the CLI case when the dependency is absent. Constants ROOT through CLIENT_COPY_DIR pin every directory the script touches relative to the repository root, so callers can override them in tests.
blocks.title: Imports, path constants, and schema roots

blocks.text: load_jsonl reads a JSONL file line by line and raises a ValueError that names the file and the offending line number. iter_v1_documents yields all *.json from protocol/v1 (schemas first, then tools/). _registry() builds the referencing.Registry once and caches it; _envelope_validator() builds and caches the Draft 2020-12 validator for the message envelope.
blocks.title: Loading and registry construction

blocks.text: Issue is a frozen dataclass whose __str__ formats path, keyword, and message into a readable single line. validate_message runs the cached envelope validator and optionally strips additionalProperties errors (never on payload/input). validate_tool_input looks the tool up in the v0 catalog and returns issues from its input_schema; an unrecognised name is immediately a problem.
blocks.title: Issue dataclass and the two public validation entry points

blocks.text: units() expands run_event into its subtypes (run_event:token, run_event:state_changed, etc.) so each classifiable unit has a distinct name. data_class_units() and secret_fields() let test suites discover which units carry content versus metadata and which top-level fields must never be logged.
blocks.title: Schema introspection: units, data classes, secrets

blocks.anchor: def walk(schema, where: str = "") -> Iterator[tuple[str, dict]]:
blocks.text: walk() yields every sub-schema dict with its location as a /‑joined path, covering properties, $defs, items, allOf/anyOf/oneOf, and the if/then/else keywords but deliberately skipping plain key names so a property called 'type' is not confused with a schema keyword. property_names and iter_strings build on walk.
blocks.title: Schema tree walkers

blocks.text: check_tool_definition validates a tools/*.json doc against tool_definition.json and also checks that input_schema is itself a valid schema and that risk_max (if present) is strictly higher than risk. check_schemas iterates the whole v1 tree, enforcing BOM-free files with trailing newlines, correct $id and $schema, payload dispatch in envelope.json for every message type, and tool_proposed.json coverage for every tool.
blocks.title: Static checks of schemas and tool definitions

blocks.text: Maintains per-connection state (open/expecting_welcome), per-run seq counters, a set of proposed call IDs, and a set of finished call IDs. It checks that ids are unique, timestamps are non-decreasing, every hello is answered by welcome or error, server seq numbers are gapless, nothing arrives after a terminal state, and every tool call that is proposed is finished exactly once before the run ends.
blocks.title: Transcript coherence checker

blocks.text: check_fixtures verifies that all four required fixture files exist, then validates each .jsonl both per-line (validate_message) and as a whole transcript (check_transcript). check_invalid_examples reads invalid_examples.jsonl and asserts that every case is rejected AND that the rejection matches the expected JSON Schema keyword and path — so a broken example cannot accidentally pass for the wrong reason.
blocks.title: Fixture and invalid-example validation

blocks.text: compare_client_copy does a byte-for-byte file-by-file diff between protocol/v1 and the client's synced copy, returning [] silently when the copy does not yet exist. sync_client uses copy_tree to overwrite the client copy and then deletes any *.json files there that are no longer in protocol/v1; it refuses with FileNotFoundError when the m2c package directory is absent entirely.
blocks.title: Client-copy comparison and sync

blocks.anchor: def _report(title: str, problems: list[str], hint: str = "") -> bool:
blocks.text: _report prints 'ok' or 'FAIL' with a list of problems and an optional fix hint, returning True when clean. main() parses --sync-client and --check-client-copy as a mutually exclusive group; without either flag it runs all four checks in order, short-circuiting the fixture and client-copy checks when schema validation itself fails.
blocks.title: CLI runner

gotchas: jsonschema is NOT in backend/requirements.txt; install from protocol/requirements.txt separately
protocol/ is not a Python package — import the file via importlib, not `import protocol.validate`
tolerant=True still enforces every error EXCEPT additionalProperties, and never relaxes payload/input at all
_registry() and _envelope_validator() are both @lru_cache(maxsize=1); they reload if the process changes at runtime
sync_client raises FileNotFoundError (exit 2) rather than creating m2c/ from scratch — that is WP C01's job
compare_client_copy() silently returns [] when the client copy directory does not yet exist
how_it_works: Loads every *.json under protocol/v1 into a jsonschema referencing.Registry, keyed by a synthetic BASE_URI, then builds a cached Draft 2020-12 validator from envelope.json
validate_message() runs the envelope validator; tolerant mode strips additionalProperties issues except those inside payload/input
validate_tool_input() fetches the named tool from the v0 catalog and validates tool_input against its input_schema; an unrecognised tool name is immediately an error
check_transcript() replays a list of messages in order, maintaining state machines for connection lifecycle, run sequencing, seq numbering, and tool call/finish pairing
The CLI subcommands check_schemas, check_fixtures, check_invalid_examples, compare_client_copy, and sync_client compose those primitives into the four-step default run
outputs: list[Issue] or list[str] from every exported function
purpose: Owns the single authority for checking that every JSON schema under protocol/v1 is well-formed, that golden transcripts are individually valid and collectively coherent, and that the m2c client's synced copy of those schemas is byte-identical to the source. It is also the import entry point for client and server test suites that need to replay fixtures through the same validation functions. Validation fails closed: an unknown tool is always an error, and tolerant mode relaxes only the additionalProperties check for fields outside tool input.
side_effects: reads the filesystem (protocol/v1 and fixtures trees)
writes files to m2c/src/m2c/protocol/v1 when --sync-client is used
deletes stale *.json files from the client copy during sync
summary: Reference validator for the M2C protocol's wire format, golden-transcript fixtures, and tool-schema contract, runnable as a CLI or importable by test suites.
